Subject: Renewal: Helix — incremental GPU corridor plan & SLA smoothing

Hi Tracy —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Attached is the utilization report for the last 90 days and a proposed incremental "corridor" plan that smooths SLA exposures while keeping unit cost predictable. High-level summary below: 

- Observation: Peak sustained 1-minute utilization spikes across your embed/ingest clusters drive high token latency; average utilization ~38% but peaks hit 88% for short windows.
- Proposed immediate change: Add 8x A100-equivalent GPUs to the steady pool (reservation tranche) and create a 12-GPU burst corridor (reserved but preemptible at lower priority) to absorb spikes.
- Alternative: Replace 4 A100s with 8 L4s for embeddings offload (saves ~18% cost on embedding-heavy runs).

Attachments: helix-util-report-202705.pdf, proposed-fleet-matrix-helix.xlsx

Next steps I suggest: Rishi and I will finalize the exact tranche counts and cost delta; Marissa can confirm discount band. Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the plan with ops?

Best,
Aditya Rao

Aditya / Marissa —

Quick technical note and numbers (see attached matrix):

- Placement: Burst corridor will be provisioned in an isolated AZ group and marked with a separate routing policy (policy: burst-priority). Steady pool remains in primary AZs to minimize cross-AZ tails. That satisfies Helix's isolation ask.
- Routing & Offload: We recommend synchronous offload for embeddings to L4s with a TTL-based cache for KV-prefix-heavy requests; routing will be handled by a model routing rule (primary -> embed-offload) that keeps generation and embedding pipelines separate. Fallthrough to A100s is automatic on cold misses.
- Numbers (monthly effective capacity): current steady pool: 96 A100-equivalent units; proposal: +8 steady A100s + 12 burst A100s OR +8 steady A100s + 6 burst A100s + 8 L4s (embedding offload). Estimated monthly delta: +$42k (pure A100 corridor) vs +$33k (mixed with L4s).
- SLA smoothing: With corridor in place and prefix caching, we predict 70% reduction in 99th percentile token latency incidents during peak windows.

Attachments referenced: proposed-fleet-matrix-helix.xlsx (detailed rows).

If Marissa can confirm discount bands, I can produce a formal amendment for renewals and include an opt-in DocuSign.

-Rishi
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Renewal: Helix — incremental GPU corridor plan & SLA smoothing

Thanks — this is a clean plan. Helix historically needs at least a 12% discount on expanded commit to sign; we have headroom in band B (10-15%) if we compress the burst corridor term to 6 months (shorter-term burst credits) and guarantee a minimum steady commit. Proposed commercial: 8 steady A100s (36 months), 12 burst A100s (6-month corridor) at 12% discount for the first year on the incremental units.

Tracy — if this commercial looks acceptable I can draft the amendment. Ben — please add procurement SLA exception language to the amendment (we’ll need the isolation/AZ language Rishi specified).

Marissa Cole
